quote_text: I have always imagined that Paradise will be a kind of library.
reflection: What kinds of lives can a library hold that a single life cannot?
context: In “The Gifts of Poetry,” Borges turns paradise into a library: a place where every possible book and life might be held.

quote_text: Is it not a pleasure, having learned something, to try it out at due intervals?
reflection: Where could you put something you learned into practice today?
context: The opening of the Analects links study with practice, then with the pleasure of meeting friends who share the way.

quote_text: As many more individuals of each species are born than can possibly survive, a struggle for existence follows.
passage_label: On the Origin of Species, Chapter III
reflection: Which pressures decide who gets a chance to flourish?
context: Darwin is building an argument from overproduction and competition in nature toward natural selection—not offering a general slogan about personal resilience.

quote_text:
Hope is the thing with feathers
That perches in the soul.
reflection: What keeps singing in you when everything outside goes quiet?
context: Dickinson’s bird is inward: hope keeps singing in the soul even when the weather turns hard.

quote_text: Imagination is more important than knowledge. Knowledge is limited. Imagination encircles the world.
reflection: What could you imagine more freely if you still had to test it?
context: Einstein said this in an interview about scientific intuition, imagination, and testing ideas against evidence. The familiar one-line version leaves out the thought that follows.

quote_text: A man of genius makes no mistakes. His errors are volitional and are the portals of discovery.
reflection: When has a mistake become a discovery because you chose to treat it as one?
context: In Ulysses, Stephen Dedalus recasts artistic “errors” as deliberate choices that can open new paths of discovery.

quote_text: The best kind of revenge is, not to become like unto them.
reflection: What would it mean to answer harm without repeating it?
context: In this translation Marcus is reflecting on how to respond to people who offend or need correction; the passage argues for pity and gentleness over anger.

quote_text: You know also that the beginning is the most important part of any work, especially in the case of a young and tender thing.
reflection: What early influence is shaping a person before they can name it?
context: Socrates is discussing stories told to children and how early impressions shape a developing character.

quote_text: To be, or not to be, that is the question.
reflection: What helps you stay with a question that has no easy answer?
context: Hamlet’s question begins a meditation on suffering, action, and the fear of what may follow death.

quote_text: I went to the woods because I wished to live deliberately, to front only the essential facts of life.
passage_label: Walden; or, Life in the Woods
reflection: What is essential enough to deserve more of your attention?
context: Thoreau explains his experiment at Walden: simplify daily life to see what is essential, and whether life can be lived deliberately.

quote_text: All happy families are alike; each unhappy family is unhappy in its own way.
reflection: What small difference makes each family’s story its own?
context: This is the novel’s famous opening sentence. The story soon tests the idea against one family’s private grief, desire, and social judgment.

quote_text: I would venture to guess that Anon, who wrote so many poems without signing them, was often a woman.
passage_label: A Room of One’s Own, Chapter 3
reflection: Whose work might we miss because its author’s name was never recorded?
context: Woolf imagines the anonymous poet as a woman whose work survived without her name. “For most of history, Anonymous was a woman” is a popular paraphrase, not her sentence.
